Let me check Russia's response and last trilateral meeting.**Bottom line:** As of October 6, 2026, nothing has been scheduled for October 15–17. If the question were resolved today, it would resolve **NO**. The US has proposed a technical-level trilateral meeting "by the end of October," but no date or venue has been announced, and I found no public reply from Russia to that specific proposal.

**Resolution source:** I didn't open the Metaculus FAQ page itself. As generally understood, its "credible sources" definition covers major reputable news outlets and official government statements. The key requirement here is that all three governments meet in person, in the same room, during October 15–17 (UTC).

**Latest news (newest first)**
- **Oct 4, 2026:** At a press conference in Kyiv with German Chancellor Merz, Zelensky said the US is "proposing to hold some kind of meeting at the technical level in a trilateral format by the end of October". He said Ukraine is "open to the UAE or any other country proposed by the U.S. side," but wasn't sure whether Russia had received the proposal yet, and Kyiv would wait for a response. Media reports suggest the talks may take place in October in Abu Dhabi to discuss a partial ceasefire covering energy infrastructure, and a possible reopening of the Black Sea grain corridor is expected to be on the agenda.
- **Same report:** Moscow is still attacking Ukraine's power grid, and sources say Trump privately doubts Putin will agree to an energy truce before winter.
- **About Sept 13–14:** Kremlin spokesman Peskov said trilateral talks would come in "the foreseeable future. That is, presumably of course, October." Envoys Witkoff and Kushner had met Putin in Moscow and then Zelensky in Kyiv, and Witkoff said progress had been made toward a three-way meeting. Around the same time, the UAE crown prince offered to host, and Ushakov reported this positively (Sept 13).
- **Sept 12:** Kyrylo Budanov, head of Ukraine's Presidential Office, said of the next trilateral round: "We're getting ready. For October."
- **Sept:** Secretary of State Rubio said talks could resume in the coming weeks.

**History / base rates**
- 2026 trilateral rounds: Abu Dhabi on Jan 23–24 and Feb 4–5, then Geneva on 17 and 18 February 2026.
- A round planned for March 5–6 in Abu Dhabi fell through. The Kremlin said it had "no clarity" on the timing or location and pointed to the US–Iran conflict. There has been no trilateral meeting since, so about 7.5 months.
- Timelines have tended to slip. The second round was "tentatively" set for Feb 1 but actually held Feb 4–5. Dates were usually announced only a few days ahead; Geneva, for example, was announced Feb 13 for Feb 17–18.
- Each round lasted two days. A meeting that started on Oct 14 and continued into Oct 15 would still count.

**What this means for the forecast**
- The window covers 3 days of the roughly 25 left in October, and "by end of October" suggests late in the month. US-driven timelines have repeatedly slipped.
- Moscow's acceptance of this specific proposal hasn't been confirmed.
- No events are scheduled for the window. Things to watch: Kremlin (Peskov/Ushakov) confirmation of a date, Witkoff/Kushner travel, and UAE hosting announcements. Given past practice, an announcement around Oct 10–13 would be the signal.

**Prediction markets:** I didn't find any market prices for this question.

criterios: This question resolves YES if, at any time between October 15, 2026 and October 17, 2026 (inclusive, UTC), officials or negotiators representing the governments of Russia, Ukraine, and the United States convene an in-person meeting at which all three governments are represented, for the purpose of negotiating matters related to the Russia–Ukraine war, as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). The meeting may be at any level (technical/delegation level or leader level) and may be held at any venue. It resolves NO if no such in-person trilateral meeting is reported to have taken place during this window.
letra_pequena: The meeting must have representatives of all three governments physically present in the same location; a purely bilateral meeting (e.g., US–Ukraine or US–Russia only), a virtual/phone meeting, or shuttle diplomacy in which the parties never share a room does not count. A meeting that began before October 15, 2026 counts only if it is reported to still be in session on or after October 15, 2026. The content need not produce any agreement; convening the meeting is sufficient.
razonamientos:
**(a) Time left:** The window is October 15–17, 2026, which is 9–11 days from today (October 6). The outcome will be known by about October 18.

**(b) Status quo:** No meeting is scheduled for the window. If nothing changed, this resolves NO.

**(c) Reference class:**
- In 2026, US-proposed trilateral rounds have tended to slip. The second round moved from Feb 1 to Feb 4–5, and the planned March 5–6 round never happened.
- There has been no trilateral meeting for about 7.5 months despite repeated signals that talks would resume.
- Dates have typically been announced only 3–5 days ahead.
- My estimate is about 35–45% that any trilateral meeting happens in October at all. If one does, a 3-day window (effectively 4 start days, since a meeting starting Oct 14 and running into Oct 15 counts) out of the roughly 25 days left has about a 15–25% chance of overlapping. The "by end of October" framing points later in the month.
- That gives roughly 5–10%.

**(d) No scenario:** Russia stalls on replying to the US proposal, or the energy-truce talks bog down. The meeting slips to late October or November, or doesn't happen at all.

**(e) Yes scenario:** Moscow quickly accepts. Around October 11–13 the UAE announces Abu Dhabi talks for October 15–16, and technical delegations from all three countries meet in person.

**(f) Technicalities:**
- All three governments must be physically present in the same place.
- Proximity or shuttle talks, where the UAE or US moves between separate rooms, would not count.
- A meeting starting October 14 counts only if it continues into October 15 (UTC).

Probability: 6%

(a) **Time left:** Nine days until the October 15–17 window begins; the outcome will be known after it ends, subject to reporting delays.

(b) **Status quo:** No date or venue is fixed, and Russia has not publicly accepted the specific US proposal. If nothing changes, the answer is **No**.

(c) **Reference class:** For a meeting targeted only for “October,” a particular three-day window is a small part of the month. Even allowing for two-day meetings, it would capture only a minority of October start dates. The March round that fell through also argues against treating the proposed month as a commitment.

(d) **No scenario:** The parties continue discussing arrangements, but the meeting is set for later in October or slips again.

(e) **Yes scenario:** Russia accepts promptly, a venue and October 15–16 date are announced on short notice, and all three delegations meet in person.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** A meeting starting October 14 counts if it is still in session on October 15. Bilateral meetings, calls, and shuttle diplomacy do not count without representatives of all three governments physically meeting together.

I give the proposed October restart some weight, but more weight to the absence of a confirmed date so close to this narrow window.

Probability: 12%

(a) **Time left:** The window opens in nine days. The outcome should be knowable after October 17, subject to reporting delays.

(b) **Status quo:** No meeting is scheduled, so if nothing changes, the answer is **NO**.

(c) **Reference class:** Three trilateral rounds took place earlier in 2026, but none has occurred in roughly seven and a half months. That is a low base rate for any particular three-day window. The renewed October push raises it, though no date has been agreed.

(d) **NO scenario:** The parties remain willing to talk but cannot settle a date before October 18, or meet only bilaterally.

(e) **YES scenario:** Russia accepts the US proposal, and delegations convene together on October 15 or 16.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** A meeting begun before October 15 counts if it is still in session during the window. All three governments must be physically represented together; shuttle or virtual talks do not count.

The short, unscheduled window outweighs the encouraging signals about October talks generally.

Probability: 9%
